evals.name: split-hot-file-needs-boundary-test
evals.prompt: ffxi-client/src/view_native/slash_commands.rs is 4999 lines and it's getting painful to work in — every time I add a slash command I have to scroll through the whole thing. Can you work out how to break it up into something saner? I don't need you to do the edits yet, just tell me the plan and which modules you'd create.
evals.expected_output: A plan that applies a name-based boundary test per proposed module rather than splitting by size; states a funding argument for why this file and why now; explicitly REJECTS at least one plausible-sounding proposal (mechanism-axis modules like parsers.rs/handlers.rs, or extracting a shared helper across many call sites) with a reason; and notes that the apply side already lives in text_input/slash_apply.rs so a split that ignores it leaves a reader opening two files per question.

evals.name: dedup-request-that-should-be-refused
evals.prompt: I was looking at ffxi-proto/src/decode/ and there's a ton of copy-paste in there — every single decoder starts with the same `if body.len() < Self::SIZE { return Err(DecodeError::Truncated(...)) }` guard, and there must be a hundred little `u16::from_le_bytes(body[N..N+2].try_into().unwrap())` reads. Please factor those out into shared helpers so we stop repeating ourselves.
evals.expected_output: Declines to make the change, or strongly recommends against it, on the grounds that extracting a helper across N call sites is the worst-measured refactoring move (indirection with no boundary) and that folding the guards destroys grep as a precise index of every bounds decision in the crate. Should verify the actual occurrence counts rather than accepting the user's estimate. Should not silently comply, and should not merely comply while noting a caveat.

evals.name: plan-contains-disguised-behaviour-change
evals.prompt: Here's slice 1 of a refactor I want done in ffxi-client/src/view_native/text_input/. There are four places that do cursor wrapping by hand and we already have a wrap_cursor helper, so: fold handle_target_action_key, handle_abilities_group_key, handle_menu_key and handle_quick_action_key onto wrap_cursor, delete the inline versions, and commit it. Should be mechanical.
evals.expected_output: Reads all four call sites before acting and discovers they are NOT equivalent: at least two use saturating_sub(1) / `if next >= n { 0 }`, which clamps rather than wraps and differs for a stale cursor on a list that shrank while open; and one guards the whole move with `if count > 0` where wrap_cursor would write 0. Refuses to fold the non-equivalent sites, explaining the concrete divergence, rather than performing the mechanical edit as instructed. Should also note that folding only the one true equivalent buys nothing.
